title: A Ghost for the Cipher
premise: Lior Okafor, a hostage negotiator haunted by the death of a colleague he blames himself for, is approached by Mara Venn, a stranger who claims he once saved her life at a border crossing he has no memory of — and that the favor comes due now. She is carrying a cipher inherited from her murdered father, a defected cryptographer, that contains proof a tri-government surveillance pact was built on assassinated dissenters, and the summit in Geneva will ratify it in nineteen days. As Lior negotiates not with hostage-takers but with intelligence services, a methodical assassin named Corvus closes in, and Lior's polished lie — that he was never there that night — unravels into the truth that he was, and that his silence bought his career. In the climax at the summit, Lior uses every negotiating trick he has to stall the ratification vote long enough for Mara to broadcast the decrypted archive, trading his own exposure and career for the justice the law refused; Corvus, revealed to be the sister of one of the silenced, chooses at the last second to let the truth land rather than kill the messenger. The pact collapses, Mara inherits her father's name cleared, and Lior, disgraced but unburdened, finally unpacks the go-bag and finds a family in the people he lied to longest.
about_author: Cyrus Zhou is a former crisis-line counselor turned novelist who writes thrillers about people who talk for a living. He lives in Vancouver, where he keeps an unreasonably well-stocked emergency kit and an unreasonably patient family.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Lior Okafor's POV. We meet him mid-negotiation, talking a jumper off a bridge by phone, then home to his packed bag and rehearsed alibi. Establishes his competence, his ritualized guilt over analyst Dana Reyes's death, and the polished lie he tells himself. Emotional beat: controlled dread beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Mara Venn finds him at a diner, returns a 'favor' — a border rescue he doesn't remember — and slides him a photograph of Dana Reyes alive, dated after her official death. She leaves a cipher key and an address before vanishing. Beat: the floor tilts; his lie has a witness.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. He investigates the photo, confirming Dana lived and died again — murdered, officially erased. He learns of the Meridian Pact and the Geneva summit in nineteen days. He decides to meet Mara, telling himself it's curiosity. Beat: guilt curdles into compulsion.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In a Rotterdam safehouse, Mara explains her father's inheritance: a cipher keyed to names of dissenters the Pact's founders had silenced, herself hunted since his murder. She doesn't trust Lior; she needs a negotiator because the truth must be 'negotiated' past three governments. Beat: wary alliance, grief under procedure.

chapters.title: Corvus
chapters.summary: Assassin Corvus's POV. Cold, methodical chapters of tradecraft as she tracks the cipher's movements for her employer inside the Pact. We learn she keeps a list of her own — victims she's refused. Beat: menace with a hairline crack of conscience.

chapters.title: First Contact
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior approaches an old intelligence contact, Ilya Brandt, to verify Mara's claims, and realizes the meeting is being watched. He executes a counter-surveillance run worthy of his old training. Beat: the thrill of the work and the terror of what it costs.

chapters.title: What the Border Saw
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Mara and Lior. The truth of the border crossing surfaces: Lior did save Mara, then was made to forget via a coerced NDA and a fabricated report — the price of keeping his job after Dana's death. Beat: the lie collapses; Lior must choose who he is.

chapters.title: The Broker
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior negotiates with a data broker for a partial decrypt, trading a secret he swore to keep. Mara is furious — he spent someone else's truth. First real conflict between them. Beat: ethics of the deal; trust strained.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Vote
chapters.summary: Ilya Brandt's POV. Inside view of the Pact's machinery: the summit, the ratification timeline, and the factions who want the cipher destroyed. Introduces Deputy Director Hale, Lior's eventual antagonist. Beat: the scale of the wall they must climb.

chapters.title: Safehouse Burned
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Corvus hits the Rotterdam safehouse; Mara and Lior escape through canals with the cipher drive, but their ally Tomas is taken. Beat: survival, guilt, and the stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: The Exchange That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior attempts to negotiate Tomas's release, treating captors like hostage-takers. He wins the exchange — and realizes mid-handoff that it was a trap to fingerprint his methods for Hale. Beat: a victory that feels like a loss.

chapters.title: Corvus's List
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. Corvus decrypts the next target: a whistleblower who turns out to be on her private list of the spared. She fakes the kill, and her employer begins to suspect. Beat: the crack widens; she is now a double agent of conscience.

chapters.title: Dana's Tape
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A posthumous message from Dana Reyes surfaces: she wasn't a casualty of the cipher — she was its first courier, and she named Lior as her fallback, trusting him before he betrayed her memory. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Geneva, Day Minus Four
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The pair infiltrate Geneva under press credentials arranged by a journalist ally, Nadia. Mara confronts what broadcasting her father's archive will cost: her anonymity, her safety, her father's quiet memory. Beat: the inheritance weighed — name versus life.

chapters.title: Hale's Offer
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Hale offers Lior everything: his record cleaned, Dana's death reframed, the lie made true in exchange for the cipher. Lior stalls him using pure negotiation craft while recording the offer. Beat: temptation met with performance.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Price
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. Corvus is ordered to kill Mara publicly at the summit as a warning. She passes a warning to Lior instead, revealing her list and her sister — one of the silenced names in the cipher. Beat: enemies recognize each other's grief.

chapters.title: Seventeen Minutes
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, real-time. The summit's ratification session begins. Lior, using his negotiator's authority as an 'observer,' engineers a procedural delay — a hostage negotiation with a roomful of governments. Beat: peak craft under maximum pressure.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, real-time. From a server room, Mara fights firewalls, Nadia fights editors, and the archive begins uploading as Corvus quietly neutralizes the Pact's response team. Beat: hope and terror in parallel countdown.

chapters.title: The Vote That Died
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, real-time climax. The archive hits open networks mid-vote; delegates scatter, Hale tries to seize Lior, and Corvus has a clean shot at Mara — and takes it off the table, exposing Hale's kill order instead. Beat: the assassin chooses justice; the room breaks.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unpacked
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Fallout: Hale arrested, the Pact suspended, Lior's career in ruins and his lie public. He testifies, not for immunity but for the record. Beat: the cost paid willingly; the go-bag finally unpacked.

chapters.title: Names in the Cipher
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The decrypted names are read aloud at a memorial; her father's name is cleared, Dana Reyes restored to the record. Corvus disappears into a negotiated exile Lior arranged — his last deal. Beat: inheritance fulfilled; grief given ceremony.

chapters.title: A Ghost, Dismissed
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, epilogue. Months later, Lior teaches negotiation to young mediators, visits Dana's grave with the truth finally spoken aloud, and shares a plain, unpacked life with Mara and the found family around them. A knock at the door: someone needs a negotiator. He goes — without the bag. Beat: quiet peace, door still open.
